conventions.convention: Finite Weyl data: Φ ⊆ E∖{0} is a finite reduced crystallographic root system spanning a positive definite real space E (integral pairings ⟨β,α∨⟩ ∈ Z, reflection stability, only ±α among the scalar multiples of a root); positivity comes from a regular t with Φ+ = {α : (t,α) > 0}, simple roots are the positive roots not expressible as a sum of two positive roots, Inv(w) = {α ∈ Φ+ : wα ∈ Φ−}, reduced means least simple-letter length; Q = ΣZα, Q∨ = ΣZα∨ with α∨ = 2α/(α,α), P = {λ : (λ,α∨) ∈ Z for all α}, Q+ = Σ_i Z≥0 α_i, and μ ≤ λ iff λ − μ ∈ Q+; the empty root system on E = 0 with W = {1} is allowed, and existence of t, the simple basis, generation of W and every lattice/chamber/stabilizer assertion are explicitly deferred to later items, not assumed by the definition.

Chambers: C = {x : (x,α_i) > 0 for all i}, C̄ = {x : (x,α_i) ≥ 0 for all i}, general chambers are the connected components of E minus the union of the root hyperplanes, and a weight is dominant iff it lies in P ∩ C̄; the closed-chamber representative and stabilizer assertions are proved later (in lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers), not built into the definition.

Strong Bruhat order is the ordered-subword relation on reduced expressions (u ≤ v iff some reduced expression for v contains a reduced expression for u as an ordered subword of ℓ(u) letters; the empty subword represents 1); the item proves independence of the chosen reduced expression and equivalence with the saturated root-reflection-chain description, and states that no abstract Coxeter presentation, weak order or inversion-set containment is substituted.

Orbit sums m_λ = Σ_{μ∈Wλ} e^μ sum each distinct orbit element exactly once (stabilizers do not multiply coefficients, so wall weights acquire no factor), m_0 = e^0 = 1, and C[P] consists of finitely supported sums with basis e^μ and multiplication e^μe^ν = e^{μ+ν}.

Polynomial action and coinvariants: (g·f)(v) = f(g^{-1}v); R = S^G, R+ = ⊕_{d>0} R_d, I = SR+ (finite sums fp with f ∈ S, p ∈ R+), coinvariant algebra S/I; Reynolds operator R(f) = |G|^{-1}Σ_{g∈G} g·f is a graded R-linear projection; polynomial-function faithfulness over C, boundary cases V = 0 and G = {1}, and homogeneous decomposition of invariants are fixed here.

Weyl discriminant: Δ = Π_{α∈Φ+} ℓ_α with ℓ_α(v) = (α,v) extended complex bilinearly on V = E⊗_R C, one factor per distinct reflecting hyperplane (degree = |Φ+|), rank zero gives Δ = 1 and the empty arrangement, and w·Δ = det(w)Δ.

Finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra: Jacobi bracket axioms, D^{j+1}g = [D^jg,D^jg], solvable iff some D^jg = 0, semisimple iff no nonzero solvable ideal (the zero algebra is semisimple); B(x,y) = tr_g(ad_x ad_y) with semisimple nondegeneracy proved later, not assumed; S(g) is a polynomial algebra via a finite basis, S^g = {p : ad_x p = 0 for every x}, I = S·S^g_+ is graded and adjoint-stable.

Rank-one sl2 normalization: [h,e] = 2e, [h,f] = −2f, [e,f] = h, with V_m of basis v_0,…,v_m and h v_k = (m−2k)v_k, f v_k = v_{k+1}, e v_k = k(m−k+1)v_{k−1}, missing endpoint vectors zero; the zero representation is the empty sum, and fe, ef act by k(m−k+1), (k+1)(m−k).

Kostant harmonics: D_x is the constant-coefficient derivation with D_x(y) = B(x,y) on generators, D_p = p(∂) for p ∈ S, and H = {h ∈ S : D_p h = 0 for every p ∈ S^g_+}; homogeneous positive-degree invariants suffice to test; H_d = I_d^⊥ for the Fischer pairing (D_pq)(0); the graded complement S_d = H_d ⊕ I_d is a separate theorem and is not inferred from complex bilinear nondegeneracy.

Kac–Moody Cartan data: row-coroot convention α_j(h_i) = a_ij with a minimal realization of dimension 2n − rank A and independent coroots, and the dual Weyl actions s_iλ = λ − λ(h_i)α_i, s_i h = h − α_i(h)h_i with α_i(h_i) = 2 (no finiteness or Coxeter presentation of W is assumed).

Integral and dominant integral weights: P = {λ ∈ h* : λ(h_i) ∈ Z for every i}, P+ = {λ ∈ P : λ(h_i) ≥ 0 for every i}; zero labels are allowed, the zero functional is dominant integral, only simple-coroot labels are constrained — complementary Cartan values are unrestricted and P need not be a lattice.

Integrability: V is a weight module (V = ⊕_{μ∈h*}V_μ) and every e_i and f_i acts locally nilpotently, both conditions independently, with exponents depending on i and the vector; no uniform exponent, no finite-dimensional weight spaces, no bounded-above support and no finite generation; the zero module is integrable.

Real root/coroot sign and inversion data: Δre = {wα_i : w ∈ W, 1 ≤ i ≤ n}, Δ∨,re = {wh_i}; a real coroot is positive when its coordinates in the independent family (h_i) are nonnegative integers and negative when its negative is positive; Inv(w) = {β ∈ Δ∨,re_+ : wβ ∈ −Δ∨,re_+}, N(λ) = {β ∈ Δ∨,re_+ : λ(β) < 0}, ℓ(w) the least word length; finiteness of Inv(w) and the one-sign property are supplied by the sign lemma rather than presumed.

Intrinsic affine level: for an indecomposable affine GCM, b is the unique positive integer vector with A^t b = 0 and gcd_i b_i = 1, the central coroot is c_A = Σ_i b_i h_i, and the level of a cyclic highest-weight module of weight λ is the scalar λ(c_A); no loop-model normalization is included.

Green setting: all modules are finite-dimensional left modules and indecomposable means nonzero; X = {P ∩ ^gP : g ∈ G∖H}, Y = {H ∩ ^gP : g ∈ G∖H}; Q ≤_K F iff some x ∈ K and T ∈ F satisfy ^xQ ≤ T; Z = {Q ≤ P : Q ≰_G X}; family-projectivity quantifies over indecomposable summands (zero module qualifies, including the empty family); 'vertex in Z' means a vertex literally in Z; AC is stated separately where used.

AC bookkeeping: the complete-reducibility, tensor-product, Green-correspondence and Green-example items carry an explicit A1 assuming AC (declaring def-axiom-of-choice), used for the finite-length decomposition chain (Krull–Schmidt), the AC-only relative-1/projectivity identification, and the simultaneous basis choices in singular weight spaces; the finite Weyl, integrability, Casimir and affine-level arguments are asserted choice-free, prop-integrable-weight-sets-and-multiplicities-are-weyl-invariant using AC only to interpret multiplicities as cardinalities of bases.

Category O (imported convention, not fixed by an owned item): finite-dimensional weight spaces with support in a finite union ∪_j(λ_j − Q+), closed under submodules and quotients, with finite upper sets; no finite generation or finite length included.

load_bearing.statement: "Let E be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a positive definite symmetric bilinear form. A finite reduced crystallographic root system is a finite subset Φ ⊆ E∖{0} spanning E, such that for every α,β ∈ Φ the integer ⟨β,α∨⟩ = 2(β,α)/(α,α) is integral, the reflection s_α preserves Φ, and the only scalar multiples of α in Φ are α,−α. ... The root and coroot groups are Q = Σ Zα and Q∨ = Σ Zα∨. The weight group is P = {λ ∈ E : (λ,α∨) ∈ Z for all α ∈ Φ} ... write μ ≤ λ when λ−μ ∈ Q+. The open and closed positive chambers are C = {x : (x,α_i) > 0} and C̄ = {x : (x,α_i) ≥ 0}. A weight is dominant if it belongs to P ∩ C̄."

"the module M_A(λ) represents a specified highest vector of weight λ: for every g(A)-module V and vector v ∈ V with hv = λ(h)v and n+v = 0, there is exactly one module map M_A(λ) → V sending 1⊗1 to v. The image is U(g)v. The Verma module belongs to O, is nonzero, and has formal character ch M_A(λ) = e^λ Π_{α∈Δ+}(1−e^{−α})^{−dim g_α}."

"regular vectors t exist, W is finite, and the simple positive roots are a basis of E. Every root has integral coordinates in this basis of one sign. ... The simple reflections generate W, and every root is the image of a simple root under their group. The simple coroots similarly form an integral basis of the coroot group, and P is the lattice generated by their dual basis; W preserves Q,Q∨,P."

"Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and G ≤ GL(V) finite. Write S = C[V] = Sym(V*) ... Define (g·f)(v) = f(g^(-1)v) ... Let R = S^G = {f ∈ S : g·f = f for every g ∈ G}, R+ = ⊕_{d>0}R_d, I = SR+. The invariant polynomial algebra is R; the coinvariant algebra is the graded quotient S/I. ... The Reynolds operator is R(f) = |G|^(-1)Σ_{g∈G} g·f."

"P = {λ ∈ h* : λ(h_i) ∈ Z for every i}, P+ = {λ ∈ P : λ(h_i) ≥ 0 for every i}. Elements of P are integral weights; elements of P+ are dominant integral weights. ... complementary Cartan values are unrestricted; P need not be a discrete lattice in h*."

"A module V is integrable if it is a weight module and every e_i,f_i acts locally nilpotently. ... Finite-dimensional weight spaces, bounded-above support and finite generation are not part of integrability. Nor is a uniform nilpotence exponent required. The zero module is integrable ... Both raising and lowering conditions are required, independently."

"For Q ≤ P, the following are equivalent: Q ≤_G X, Q ≤_H X, Q ≤_H Y. Every member of X is proper in P, and P ∈ Z. If Q,R ∈ Z and ^gQ = R, then g ∈ H. No member of Y contains an H-conjugate of a member of Z."

"X = {P ∩ ^gP : g ∈ G∖H}, Y = {H ∩ ^gP : g ∈ G∖H}. ... Q ≤_K F if some x ∈ K and T ∈ F satisfy ^xQ ≤ T. ... Z = {Q ≤ P : Q ≰_G X}. ... Having a vertex in Z means that at least one vertex ... is literally a member of Z."

"The algebra is solvable if some D^j g = 0, and semisimple if it has no nonzero solvable ideal. The zero algebra is semisimple. ... Its Killing form is B(x,y) = tr_g(ad_x ad_y); its nondegeneracy in the semisimple case is proved in the next lemma, not assumed here. ... Define S^g = {p : ad_x p = 0 for every x ∈ g} and S^g_+ = ⊕_{d>0}(S^g ∩ S_d). The invariant ideal I = S S^g_+ ... is graded and stable under all adjoint derivations."

"There is a decomposition g = h ⊕ ⊕_{α∈Φ} g_α ... where the nonzero weights Φ are finite, span h*, and each root space has dimension one. ... The real span h_R of the h_α is a real form of h on which B is positive definite. On E = h_R* with the dual form, Φ is a finite reduced crystallographic root system and h_α is its coroot."

"Every finite-dimensional complex representation of the relations [h,e] = 2e, [h,f] = −2f, [e,f] = h is a finite direct sum of the simple modules V_m, m ∈ Z_{≥0}. The module V_m has basis v_0,…,v_m and action h v_k = (m−2k)v_k, f v_k = v_{k+1}, e v_k = k(m−k+1)v_{k−1}, where missing endpoint vectors are zero."

"Every W-orbit in E has exactly one point in C̄. For η ∈ C̄, its stabilizer is generated by those simple reflections s_i with (η,α_i) = 0. The group acts simply transitively on open chambers. There is a unique longest element w_0, characterized by w_0Φ+ = Φ−; it has length |Φ+| and satisfies w_0^2 = 1. In particular every weight orbit has a unique dominant weight."

"the Verma module M_A(λ) has a unique maximal proper submodule N_λ. The quotient L_A(λ) = M_A(λ)/N_λ is nonzero, simple and highest weight λ. Every simple module generated by a nonzero highest vector of weight λ is isomorphic to this quotient."

"let M be an indecomposable kG-module with vertex Q ∈ Z. Then Res_H^G M ≅ U ⊕ E, where U is indecomposable with vertex Q, occurs once, E is relatively Y-projective, and M | Ind_H^G U. No other summand has a vertex in Z."

"For every dominant integral λ, L(λ) is finite-dimensional, its support is contained in λ−Q+, its top weight has multiplicity one, and all its weight multiplicities are W-invariant. Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple g-module is exactly one such L(λ) up to isomorphism, with a unique dominant integral highest weight."

"ch L(λ) = m_λ + Σ_{μ dominant, μ<λ} n_{λ,μ}m_μ, where the coefficients are nonnegative integers and the support is finite. The inverse expansion expressing m_λ in these characters has integral coefficients, coefficient one at ch L(λ), and finite support on the same dominant ideal. In particular the characters form a basis of C[P]^W."

concerns.concern: Of the five page-level requires declared for this page (semisimple-lie-algebras-cohomology-and-levi-theory, cartan-subalgebras-and-root-space-decompositions, root-systems-dynkin-diagrams-and-cartan-killing-classification, highest-weight-theory-for-complex-semisimple-lie-algebras, depth-and-cohen-macaulay-modules), only depth-and-cohen-macaulay-modules exists as a file under library/; the other four have no page file anywhere in the repository and are absent from research/phase-2-next-20-scope-ledger.json, so they are not built by this run either. Every item-level dependency of the page resolves to a published item, so this is a page-metadata/ownership reconciliation item (the dispatch claim that every declared requires points at published content is not satisfied on disk), not a defect of the mathematical content.

The closing page prose still reads 'The companion gives complete direct calculations for S3 Bruhat order, the A2 coinvariant quotient and the sl2 harmonic decomposition. These special cases do not assert the unresolved general results.' The general results are no longer unresolved on this page: strong exchange and both Bruhat descriptions, Chevalley–Shephard–Todd for finite Weyl groups, the unitriangular characters, local Chevalley restriction, the harmonic complement and the Kostant decomposition are all proved by items of this same page. Calling them 'unresolved' is stale wording that can mislead a reader about the page's own state.

Step 3.1 asserts 'Relative T-projectivity supplies the counit splitting V | Ind_T^L Res_T^L V from F4', but F4 only lists Mackey, transitivity, preservation of summands, vertex containment and finite summand extraction (lem-relative-projectivity-mackey-intersections-for-finite-modules), none of which states the counit form V | Ind_T^L Res_T^L V of relative projectivity; that equivalence is the (nontrivial) Higman form, and thm-higman-criterion-for-relative-projectivity is not in this item's fact list (it is only named indirectly in the Definition of a vertex). A reader closes the step in seconds via Higman, which the item's F1 names as the detection tool, but the citation as written attributes more to F4 than the cited statement contains.

alerts.finding: The definition body assumes AC — 'Assuming the Axiom of Choice, when H = 1 a basis B of W gives Ind_1^G W ≅ ⊕_B kG, which may have infinite rank. Thus a relatively 1-projective module is projective. ... Hence, under Choice, relative 1-projectivity recovers ordinary projectivity' — but its front matter declares only 'deps: [def-projective-module, thm-projective-module-characterizations]' and omits def-axiom-of-choice, contrary to CLAUDE.md rule 11 ('State the assumption in the item contract ... declaring def-axiom-of-choice as a dependency'). The mathematics is unaffected; the three owned items that invoke the under-AC comparison (ex-green-correspondence-for-a-trivial-intersection-subgroup, ex-green-correspondence-identity-boundaries, and the AC clause used to place nontrivial-vertex = nonprojective in the TI example) each carry their own A1 AC declaration, so no owned bookkeeping gap propagates from this.

The proof uses [L1] 'Finite-dimensional modules have finite length ([[thm-composition-series-iff-noetherian-and-artinian]])', but that supplier's title and statement read 'A module has a composition series if and only if it is Noetherian and Artinian, the converse using dependent choice' and it declares deps [..., def-dependent-choice, def-axiom-of-choice]. The present item declares deps [def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module, thm-composition-series-iff-noetherian-and-artinian] and neither def-dependent-choice nor def-axiom-of-choice, so the DC/AC hypothesis of the clause it uses is not propagated (CLAUDE.md rule 11). The statement is true and admits a choice-free dimension induction, so this is an undeclared-hypothesis interface defect, not a false claim; the five owned Green consumers of this item (lem-green-vertex-retention-and-inducing-lift, lem-green-mackey-intersections-force-proper-vertices, lem-green-restriction-has-one-distinguished-summand, lem-green-induction-has-one-distinguished-summand, ex-green-correspondence-for-a-trivial-intersection-subgroup) each assume AC explicitly in A1 and attribute it to exactly this chain-condition converse.

This item's front matter reads 'status: draft' and 'origin: pipeline', while its home page library/representation-theory/blocks-defect-groups-and-the-brauer-homomorphism.md is 'status: published' and lists it among its items (every item listed on that page reads status: draft, so the page as a whole is in a published-page/draft-items state). Five owned Green items declare it as a dependency and consume its Mackey, transitivity, vertex-containment and summand-extraction clauses (lem-green-vertex-retention-and-inducing-lift, lem-green-mackey-intersections-force-proper-vertices, lem-green-restriction-has-one-distinguished-summand, lem-green-induction-has-one-distinguished-summand, lem-green-distinguished-summands-are-mutually-inverse).
